text:
Today, tax automation is organized around a shared `TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations` core with vendor namespaces behind a registry. **Instead is the only registered adapter.** GruntWorx already has a provider enum value, but that does not make it operational; Juno remains on a legacy path outside the registry.

**The vendor-neutral ports**

The shared layer owns these operations:

| Area | Shared responsibility |
|---|---|
| Authorization and connections | Start authorization, complete connection, select/switch provider, report connection and capabilities, disconnect, renew, verify, and revoke grants |
| Export | Authorize access, validate documents against capabilities, create/reuse the preparation and send records, then dispatch to the adapter |
| Status ingestion | Accept an adapter’s normalized processing status, enforce valid transitions, and broadcast the result |
| Recovery | Resume failed sends after reconnection; sweep uploaded documents whose processing status needs reconciliation |
| Preparation lifecycle | Find/create preparations, supply form prefills, merge contacts, and delete preparations |
| Firm lifecycle | Disconnect grants across vendors and clean up both shared and adapter records |

The export boundary is particularly clear: the core hands the adapter a preparation and shared send records; the adapter decides how those become vendor API calls. See [ExportAsync](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:53). Incoming vendor statuses must already be translated into the shared vocabulary before entering [Documents::UpdateStatus](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/update_status.rb:9).

**Registration and the adapter contract**

[Registry](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/registry.rb:3) contains two explicit maps:

```ruby
ADAPTERS = {instead: TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead}.freeze
FEATURE_FLAGS = {instead: :tax_automations_instead}.freeze
```

Dispatch can resolve an adapter from an explicit provider or from the firm’s settings. An unknown provider raises `UnknownProviderError`. The feature flag controls whether a provider is offered; a provider without a flag entry is available to every firm.

The effective namespace contract comes from production dispatch sites, including background jobs:

| Adapter member | What the core expects |
|---|---|
| `Connection` | Firm lookup, usable/connected scopes, shared grant lifecycle and token storage, `.capabilities`, and normal ActiveRecord queries |
| `Client.new(connection)` | Shared OAuth operations, including `renew!` and `revoke_tokens!`; the shared presigned-upload path also calls `upload_to_signed_target` |
| `Authorizations::Create.call(user, actor, provider, return_url)` | Begin the vendor’s authorization ceremony |
| `Connections::Create.call(user, actor, provider, params)` | Complete authorization and return the connection |
| `ExportAsync.call(user, actor, tax_preparation, tax_automation_documents:)` | Start delivery of the shared send records |
| `Documents::ReconcileStatusesAsync.call(user, actor, connection, {tax_automation_document_ids:})` | Reconcile processing status from the background sweep |
| `MergeForContact.call(user, actor, firm_id, source_contact_id, target_contact_id)` | Merge vendor-owned records |
| `DestroyForTaxPreparations.call(user, actor, firm_id, tax_preparations)` | Delete vendor records associated with preparations |
| `DestroyForFirm.call(user, actor, firm_id)` | Clean up the vendor’s firm-owned records |

These services use the existing service-result convention: callers inspect `failed?`, `errors`, and `data`.

The background contract matters: reconciliation calls the adapter directly, and keep-alive iterates **all registered adapters**, querying their connected grants. See [reconciliation dispatch](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/reconcile_sweep_worker.rb:34) and [keep-alive](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/connections/keep_alive_worker.rb:16).

Instead’s `Client` subclasses `BaseClient`, which includes `TokenRefreshable`. It declares OAuth coordinates and implements vendor API vocabulary, headers, and error interpretation. Thus, the current shared connection abstraction is specifically **OAuth-oriented**, including access and refresh tokens. See [Instead::Client](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/client.rb:3).

**The capability passport**

The passport is a typed `Dry::Struct` returned by **`Connection.capabilities` on the class**. It describes the vendor and requires no connection row.

Its structure is:

```text
Capabilities
  terms[]
    return_type
    accepted_file_formats[]
    max_file_size_mb
  supported_tax_years[]
```

File terms belong to each return type, so a provider can accept different formats or sizes for different forms. Supported return types are derived from `terms`; there is no second list to maintain.

An adapter supplies private class methods `capability_terms` and `supported_tax_years`. Construction rejects malformed values and duplicate return-type declarations. Extensions must be canonical lowercase strings, size limits positive integers, and years between 2000 and the current year plus one. Missing implementations fail lazily when `.capabilities` is called. See [HasCapabilities](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/has_capabilities.rb:3).

The passport drives both export validation and the API’s form choices. The serializer exposes `tax_years` and enriched `return_types`, each with `value`, `name`, personal/business `type`, `file_types`, and `file_size_limit`. The size is measured using Rails’ `.megabytes` conversion. See [validation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export/validate_documents.rb:108) and [serialization](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/serializers/tax_preparation/base/tax_automations/connection_serializer.rb:61).

Instead currently declares all 11 mapped return types, configured file formats and size limits, and the current tax year plus the previous two years.

**The data model**

| Record | Role |
|---|---|
| `FirmSettings` | One row per firm: selected provider and external tenant/account binding. Provider enum: `juno: 0`, `gruntworx: 1`, `instead: 2` |
| Shared `TaxPreparation` | Preparation envelope with firm, client, optional contact, year, return type, EIN, and business name. Still physically stored in `juno_tax_preparations` |
| Shared `Document` | Send record joining a TaxDome document to a preparation, provider, and return type; owns upload and processing state |
| `Instead::Connection` | One grant per firm, staff creator, encrypted tokens and expiries, grant state, and PKCE ceremony fields |
| `Instead::Entity` | Vendor entity UUID/type, local client/contact linkage, source, and synchronization/archive information |
| `Instead::Document` | Vendor-specific extension of one shared send record: Instead entity, file UUID, and path |

A preparation is reused by **firm + client + contact + year**; changing its return type updates that envelope. Each send separately snapshots its return type and provider, preserving where that file was sent. Send uniqueness is **firm + preparation + document + provider + return type**. See [preparation reuse](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparations/find_or_create.rb:92) and [send creation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:212).

The shared send has two state machines:

- Upload: `waiting`, `uploading`, `uploaded`, `failed`.
- Processing: `sent`, `processing`, `processed`, `error`, `archived`, `exceeded`.

Vendor-specific identifiers stay in adapter tables; common progress and failure reasons stay in the [shared Document model](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/document.rb:3).

For GruntWorx, the existing extension point is therefore substantial: the enum slot exists, but registration, the namespace contract, capability declarations, and vendor persistence/transport still need implementations. Juno’s remaining table names and associations also show that the migration to this shared architecture is still incomplete.
